the-nusa-penida-resort-spa.description:
Experience unparalleled luxury on the edge of the world. The Nusa Penida Resort & Spa sits on the quiet north-west coast between Toya Pakeh and Ped, a sanctuary of tranquility with sweeping views across the Badung Strait to Bali’s volcanoes. Designed for the discerning traveler, the resort blends modern elegance with authentic Balinese charm.

Days start with sunrise over Mount Agung from your private balcony and end with candle-lit dinners on the cliff terrace. In between, swim in the cascading infinity pool, unwind with a traditional boreh massage in the spa pavilions, or let our concierge arrange snorkeling with manta rays and private drivers to Kelingking and Diamond Beach.

  • Infinity pool and sunset bar overlooking the Indian Ocean
  • Balinese spa with four treatment pavilions
  • Free fast-boat pick-up from Toya Pakeh harbor

highlights.title: Infinity pool above the strait
highlights.body: A 30-metre infinity edge looks straight across to Mount Agung — at its best at sunrise and during the golden hour.

highlights.title: Balinese spa rituals
highlights.body: Four open-air pavilions offer boreh scrubs, flower baths and traditional massage using island-grown coconut oil.

highlights.title: Ocean-to-table dining
highlights.body: The cliff terrace serves the day’s catch from Toya Pakeh fishermen alongside Balinese classics and a long wine list.

highlights.title: Seamless island transfers
highlights.body: We meet every fast boat at Toya Pakeh harbor and can book your onward Penida Gili crossing at reception.

policies.label: Breakfast
policies.value: Included for all room types, 7:00–10:30 AM

policies.label: Harbor transfer
policies.value: Free pick-up from Toya Pakeh harbor

policies.label: Children
policies.value: Welcome; under 6 stay free using existing beds

policies.label: Good to know
policies.value: Reef-safe sunscreen is provided at the pool

meru-resort-spa.description:
Meru Resort & Spa is a hideaway of garden villas just above Crystal Bay, one of Nusa Penida’s calmest and clearest bays. Thatched pavilions, frangipani gardens and private plunge pools make it a favourite for honeymooners and anyone who wants the beach at their doorstep.

Walk five minutes downhill for morning snorkeling over coral gardens, return for a long breakfast by the pool and spend the afternoon with a massage in the open-air spa. At sunset the beach club lights its lanterns and the whole bay turns gold.

  • Garden pool villas with outdoor bathtubs
  • Beach club on Crystal Bay with sun loungers
  • Daily snorkel trips to Crystal Bay and Gamat Bay

gallery.alt: Crystal Bay seen from the resort hill
Beach club loungers on the bay

highlights.title: Steps from Crystal Bay
highlights.body: A short garden path leads to the white sand and the reef — the best snorkeling on the island is right here.

highlights.title: Villas with plunge pools
highlights.body: Every villa hides behind its own stone wall, with a plunge pool, sun deck and an outdoor rain shower.

highlights.title: Sunset beach club
highlights.body: Lanterns, fresh coconuts and grilled seafood as the sun drops behind Bali’s Bukit peninsula.

highlights.title: Mola-mola season trips
highlights.body: From July to October our dive partner runs early boats to spot the giant sunfish at Crystal Bay.

policies.label: Breakfast
policies.value: Included, served in the pavilion or in-villa

policies.label: Harbor transfer
policies.value: Shared shuttle from Toya Pakeh harbor (IDR 75,000)

policies.label: Good to know
policies.value: Roads to Crystal Bay are steep — we recommend our shuttle over scooters

grand-hyatt-resort-spa.description:
Set on the Sanur beachfront along Jalan Danau Tamblingan, Grand Hyatt Resort & Spa is the easiest base for island hopping: the Sanur fast-boat harbor is five minutes away, yet the resort feels a world apart with lagoon pools, palm-shaded gardens and a calm reef-protected beach.

Spend the night before your early crossing in an ocean-view room, take the free shuttle to the harbor in the morning, and come back to Sanur’s cafés, sunrise beach walks and the spa after your trip to Nusa Penida, Lembongan or the Gilis.

  • Lagoon pools and a quiet stretch of Sanur beach
  • Free shuttle to the Sanur fast-boat harbor
  • Luggage storage while you explore the islands

highlights.title: Five minutes to the boats
highlights.body: Our shuttle leaves for the Sanur harbor before every morning departure, so you never miss the calm-water crossing.

highlights.title: Reef-protected beach
highlights.body: Sanur’s outer reef keeps the water flat — perfect for paddle boarding at sunrise and for families with young children.

highlights.title: Luggage minding
highlights.body: Travel light to the islands: leave big bags with the concierge free of charge for up to seven nights.

highlights.title: Sanur at your doorstep
highlights.body: The beachfront promenade, night market and dozens of cafés are an easy walk from the lobby.

policies.label: Breakfast
policies.value: Buffet breakfast from 6:00 AM for early boats

policies.label: Good to know
policies.value: Luggage storage is free while you visit the islands

semabu-hills-hotel-nusa-penida.description:
High on the green slopes above Ped, Semabu Hills Hotel trades beachfront bustle for jungle calm. Rooms open onto tropical gardens and the hotel’s signature tiered pools, with views over the coconut groves to the sea and, on clear mornings, to Mount Agung on Bali.

It is a peaceful base for exploring the east of the island — Atuh Beach, the Thousand Islands viewpoint, the Tree House and the cave temple of Goa Giri Putri — while our kitchen cooks Balinese family recipes with vegetables from the hotel garden.

  • Tiered jungle pools with daybeds
  • Hillside rooms with garden terraces
  • Driver and scooter rental for the east-coast loop

gallery.alt: Infinity pool at sunrise with volcano view
Garden pool facing the rice fields
Tree House deck overlooking Atuh coast

highlights.title: Tiered jungle pools
highlights.body: Three spring-fed pools step down the hillside, each with daybeds shaded by frangipani and banana palms.

highlights.title: Cool hillside breezes
highlights.body: At 150 metres above the sea, evenings are fresh enough to sleep with the doors open to the garden.

highlights.title: Gateway to the east coast
highlights.body: Atuh Beach, Diamond Beach and the Tree House are a scenic 45-minute drive — we arrange early starts to beat the crowds.

highlights.title: Garden-to-table kitchen
highlights.body: Try betutu chicken, urab salad and fresh sambal made with herbs and chilies from the hotel garden.

policies.label: Harbor transfer
policies.value: Pick-up from Banjar Nyuh or Toya Pakeh (IDR 100,000 per car)

policies.label: Good to know
policies.value: The access road is steep — book our driver for luggage

batu-karang-lembongan-resort.description:
Perched on the limestone cliffs above Jungutbatu, Batu Karang Lembongan Resort looks out over the surf breaks of Nusa Lembongan to the peaks of Bali. Terraced suites, an adults-friendly cliff pool and a laid-back bar make it the island’s classic sunset spot.

Fast boats from Sanur land on the beach just below, so you can be in the pool within minutes of arriving. Rent a bicycle to cross the Yellow Bridge to Ceningan, paddle through the mangroves at dawn, or watch the waves explode at Devil’s Tear before dinner on the terrace.

  • Cliff-top pool and sunset bar
  • Ocean-view suites with private terraces
  • Bicycles, kayaks and snorkel gear free for guests

highlights.title: The best sunset on Lembongan
highlights.body: The cliff bar faces due west — the sun sets behind Bali’s volcanoes every evening of the dry season.

highlights.title: Beach landing below
highlights.body: Fast boats from Sanur arrive at Jungutbatu beach, a five-minute ride from reception with free luggage carry.

highlights.title: Free bikes and kayaks
highlights.body: Cycle the coast road to the Yellow Bridge and Ceningan or kayak the calm lagoon at high tide.

highlights.title: Surf and snorkel at the door
highlights.body: Shipwrecks, Lacerations and Playgrounds breaks are just offshore, with a reef for snorkeling at low tide.

policies.label: Breakfast
policies.value: Included, served on the cliff terrace

policies.label: Harbor transfer
policies.value: Free pick-up from Jungutbatu beach landing

policies.label: Good to know
policies.value: Wear water shoes — boats land directly on the beach

balinese-traditional-costume-rental-at-p.intro: Capture special moments wearing traditional Balinese costumes in Penglipuran Village, one of the most beautiful traditional villages in Bali.
balinese-traditional-costume-rental-at-p.description:
Experience the unique feeling of wearing premium traditional Balinese costumes and capture every moment in Penglipuran Village, a tourist village famous for its beauty, cleanliness and cultural preservation. With a backdrop of traditional houses, neatly arranged stone streets and a serene rural atmosphere, every corner of the village is a perfect photo location.

Our dressers help you choose between the elegant kebaya and kamen for women and the udeng, saput and kamen for men, complete with gold-leaf accessories and fresh frangipani. Make-up and hair styling are done on site so you step out camera-ready.

This activity suits individuals, couples, families and groups who want to experience Balinese culture up close — and bring home memories from one of the most iconic villages on the Island of the Gods.

experiences.title: Wear Premium Traditional Balinese Costumes
experiences.body: Experience wearing traditional Balinese costumes complete with elegant traditional accessories, perfect for creating an authentic and memorable look.

experiences.title: Take Photos in Penglipuran Village
experiences.body: Capture moments in one of the most beautiful villages in Bali, famous for its traditional houses, neatly arranged streets and very natural rural atmosphere.

experiences.title: Instagrammable Photos
experiences.body: Every corner of Penglipuran Village offers a beautiful and aesthetic backdrop, making every photo look more attractive and full of character.

experiences.title: Walk the Bamboo Forest
experiences.body: End your session in the cool bamboo forest behind the village — a sacred grove that has protected Penglipuran for generations.

balinese-traditional-costume-rental-at-p.important_notes:
Arrive 15 minutes early for fitting and make-up.
Please wear a simple tank top and shorts under the costume.
The village is a living community — ask before photographing residents.

gallery.alt: Barong and kris dancer on stage

barong-and-kris-dance.intro: Watch the legendary battle between the Barong and the witch Rangda — Bali’s most dramatic dance, performed to a live gamelan orchestra.
barong-and-kris-dance.description:
The Barong and Kris Dance tells the eternal story of the struggle between good and evil. The Barong, a lion-like guardian spirit, faces Rangda, the queen of demons, while entranced warriors turn their kris daggers on themselves — protected only by the Barong’s magic.

Performed every morning on an open-air stage in Batubulan, the one-hour show features elaborate masks, gold-leaf costumes and a full gamelan orchestra. A printed synopsis in English helps you follow each of the five acts.

Combine it with a visit to the stone-carving and silver workshops of Batubulan and Celuk, or continue to Ubud for lunch — our driver can tailor the half-day to you.

experiences.title: Watch the Battle of Good and Evil
experiences.body: Follow the mythical Barong as it faces the witch Rangda in a dance passed down through generations.

experiences.title: Hear a Live Gamelan Orchestra
experiences.body: Twenty musicians play bronze metallophones, gongs and drums that drive every movement of the dancers.

experiences.title: See the Kris Trance
experiences.body: Witness the dramatic finale where entranced dancers press their daggers to their chests without harm.

experiences.title: Meet the Performers
experiences.body: After the show, take photos with the Barong and Rangda dancers in full costume.

included: Hotel pick-up in South Bali (with transfer option)
barong-and-kris-dance.important_notes:
The show starts at 9:30 AM — please arrive by 9:00 AM.
Front rows fill first; seats are allocated on arrival.
Some scenes are dramatic and may frighten very young children.

gallery.alt: Farmer ploughing a rice field with cows

bali-farm-house.intro: Spend a hands-on day on a working Balinese farm — plough the paddies, plant rice, cook in a village kitchen and learn how offerings are woven.
bali-farm-house.description:
At the Bali Farm House you trade the beach for the rhythm of rural life. Guided by a farming family, you will walk the subak irrigation channels — a UNESCO-listed water-sharing system over a thousand years old — and learn how rice is grown from seed to harvest.

Roll up your trousers to plough the mud behind a pair of cows, plant seedlings in neat rows and then wash off in the spring before lunch. In the open kitchen you will grind spices for base genep and cook a home-style Balinese meal together.

The afternoon is for crafts: weave a canang sari offering from coconut leaves, feed the farm animals and taste fresh coconut, cacao and fruit straight from the garden.

experiences.title: Plough the Paddies the Traditional Way
experiences.body: Guide a pair of farm cows through the mud of the rice terrace and see how fields have been prepared for centuries.

experiences.title: Plant Rice with a Farming Family
experiences.body: Learn the rhythm of planting seedlings by hand and hear how the subak water temples share every drop.

experiences.title: Cook a Village Lunch
experiences.body: Grind fresh spices on a stone mortar and cook chicken betutu, vegetables urab and sambal matah.

experiences.title: Weave a Canang Sari Offering
experiences.body: Fold coconut leaves into the small daily offerings you see everywhere in Bali and fill them with flowers.

bali-farm-house.important_notes:
Bring a change of clothes — you will get muddy!
Activities depend on the season; harvest replaces planting from March to May.
Vegetarian cooking available on request.

kecak-uluwatu-fire-dance.intro: Watch a hundred chanting voices and the fire dance at sunset on the cliffs of Uluwatu Temple, 70 metres above the Indian Ocean.
kecak-uluwatu-fire-dance.description:
The Kecak Fire Dance at Uluwatu is one of Bali’s unforgettable evenings. As the sun sinks into the ocean, a circle of seventy bare-chested men chant cak-cak-cak in hypnotic layers, telling the Ramayana story of Prince Rama, Princess Sita and the white monkey Hanuman.

The amphitheatre sits on the edge of the cliff beside Pura Luhur Uluwatu, one of Bali’s six sacred directional temples. Arrive early to walk the cliff path, watch the surfers far below and find a seat facing the sunset.

The show ends in a blaze as Hanuman dances through burning coconut husks — a dramatic finale lit only by fire and the last glow of the sky.

experiences.title: Sunset over the Indian Ocean
experiences.body: Take your seat in the cliff-top amphitheatre as the sky turns orange behind the dancers.

experiences.title: The Ramayana in Chant
experiences.body: Seventy voices replace the gamelan, creating a hypnotic rhythm that tells the epic love story.

experiences.title: Hanuman’s Fire Finale
experiences.body: The white monkey king kicks through burning husks in the most dramatic scene of the night.

experiences.title: Visit Uluwatu Temple
experiences.body: Walk the cliff path to the 11th-century temple — and keep your sunglasses away from the monkeys!

kecak-uluwatu-fire-dance.important_notes:
The show starts at 6:00 PM; we leave South Bali around 4:00 PM.
Monkeys at the temple grab glasses and phones — keep belongings secure.
Seating is unreserved; arrive early for a sunset-facing seat.

gallery.alt: Group of manta rays near the surface

nusa-penida-snorkeling.intro: Swim with giant manta rays at Manta Bay and snorkel three coral reefs off Nusa Penida with a licensed boat crew.
nusa-penida-snorkeling.description:
This Nusa Penida Snorkeling trip takes you to the island’s most famous marine sites in one morning. Our boat leaves Toya Pakeh at 8:30 AM for Manta Bay, where reef mantas with wingspans of up to four metres glide in to feed and be cleaned.

Next comes Gamat Bay, a gentle coral slope full of parrotfish and butterflyfish; Crystal Bay with its famously clear water; and Wall Point, where sea fans and soft corals cling to the island’s steep underwater cliffs.

Our guides are in the water with every group, life jackets are provided for all swimmers and the boat carries fresh water, fruit and towels. Underwater photos are included so you can simply enjoy the moment.

experiences.title: Swim with Manta Rays
experiences.body: Float above the cleaning station at Manta Bay as the giant rays circle just metres below you.

experiences.title: Coral Gardens of Gamat Bay
experiences.body: Gentle slopes, schooling fish and hard corals in pristine condition — ideal for first-time snorkelers.

experiences.title: Crystal-Clear Crystal Bay
experiences.body: Visibility often exceeds 20 metres in this sheltered bay on the west coast.

experiences.title: Underwater Photos Included
experiences.body: Our guide films the mantas with a GoPro and shares every photo after the trip.

nusa-penida-snorkeling.important_notes:
Mantas are wild animals; sightings are very likely but not guaranteed.
Sea conditions are calmest before 11:00 AM.
Use reef-safe sunscreen and never touch the mantas or coral.

foto-adat-bali-kuta.intro: Dress in full Balinese ceremonial attire for a professional photo session in Kuta — styled, photographed and edited the same day.
foto-adat-bali-kuta.description:
Foto Adat Bali Kuta is a professional studio-and-garden photo session in full Balinese ceremonial dress, just minutes from Kuta Beach. Choose from over sixty sets of payas agung wedding attire, temple dress and dance costumes in silk and songket.

Our stylists take care of make-up, hair and the golden gelungan headdress, then the photographer guides you through poses in a carved temple-gate set, a frangipani garden and a classic studio backdrop.

You leave with 30 edited high-resolution photos delivered the same evening — a beautiful souvenir for couples, families, friends and solo travelers alike.

experiences.title: Choose Your Ceremonial Costume
experiences.body: Pick from royal wedding attire, temple dress or Legong dance costumes in silk and gold songket.

experiences.title: Professional Styling
experiences.body: Make-up, hair and gold headdress are done by stylists who dress brides for real Balinese weddings.

experiences.title: Three Photo Sets
experiences.body: Pose at a carved temple gate, in a frangipani garden and in the studio for a varied album.

experiences.title: Same-Day Edited Photos
experiences.body: Receive 30 retouched high-resolution photos by email the same evening.

foto-adat-bali-kuta.important_notes:
Sessions last about 90 minutes including styling.
Couples and groups up to 6 people can share one session.
Please arrive with clean, dry hair.

gallery.alt: Rock arch on the west coast

kelingking-west-penida-day-tour.intro: Visit Kelingking Beach, Broken Beach, Angel’s Billabong and Crystal Bay in one full day with a private driver and guide.
kelingking-west-penida-day-tour.description:
Our Kelingking & West Penida Day Tour covers the island’s four most photographed places at a relaxed pace. Your private driver meets you at the harbor and drives the winding coastal roads, so all you need to do is enjoy the views.

The day starts at Kelingking, the famous T-Rex shaped headland above a white-sand cove. Next come Broken Beach, a natural archway where the sea rushes into a circular bay, and the tidal rock pool of Angel’s Billabong.

We finish at Crystal Bay for a swim and a fresh coconut as the afternoon light softens — or, if you prefer, a quick snorkel before the return boat.

experiences.title: Kelingking T-Rex Viewpoint
experiences.body: Stand above the most photographed cliff in Indonesia — and hike down towards the beach if you dare.

experiences.title: Broken Beach & Angel’s Billabong
experiences.body: See the natural rock arch and the crystal-clear tidal pool, just a short walk apart.

experiences.title: Swim at Crystal Bay
experiences.body: Cool off in calm turquoise water at the end of the day.

experiences.title: Private Driver & Flexible Pace
experiences.body: Stay longer where you like; your driver adapts the itinerary around you.

kelingking-west-penida-day-tour.important_notes:
Wear good shoes — the Kelingking trail is steep and takes 30–40 minutes each way.
Angel’s Billabong is closed for swimming at high tide.
Bring cash for warungs and toilets.

gallery.alt: Boat gliding through the mangrove channel
Mangrove lagoon on a sunny day

lembongan-mangrove-snorkeling-trip.intro: Glide through Lembongan’s mangrove forest by traditional boat, then snorkel the coral reefs of Mangrove Point and Gamat Bay.
lembongan-mangrove-snorkeling-trip.description:
The Lembongan Mangrove & Snorkeling Trip combines Nusa Lembongan’s two natural treasures in a single half day. First, a local boatman poles you through the quiet channels of the 200-hectare mangrove forest on the island’s north-east coast.

Watch for kingfishers, mudskippers and herons as roots arch overhead, then head out to the reef at Mangrove Point for drift snorkeling over hard corals, giant clams and schools of fish — often with a passing turtle.

Depending on the tide we finish at Gamat Bay or Crystal Bay across the channel, with fruit and cold drinks served on board.

experiences.title: Traditional Mangrove Boat Ride
experiences.body: A local boatman poles you silently through the tunnels of the mangrove forest.

experiences.title: Drift Snorkel at Mangrove Point
experiences.body: Let the gentle current carry you over the reef while you watch turtles and batfish.

experiences.title: Two Reefs in One Trip
experiences.body: Add Gamat Bay or Crystal Bay depending on the tide for even more coral.

experiences.title: Small Groups
experiences.body: A maximum of eight guests per boat keeps the trip relaxed and personal.

lembongan-mangrove-snorkeling-trip.important_notes:
Mangrove tours run on the high tide — your start time is confirmed the day before.
Children from 6 years welcome with a life jacket.
Use reef-safe sunscreen only.

gallery.alt: Sea spray over the rugged cliffs

devils-tear-island-cycling.intro: Cycle the quiet roads of Nusa Lembongan and Ceningan — the Yellow Bridge, seaweed farms, Dream Beach and the crashing waves of Devil’s Tear.
devils-tear-island-cycling.description:
The Devil’s Tear & Island Cycling tour is the best way to discover Nusa Lembongan at an easy pace. With a local guide you ride comfortable bikes along coastal lanes, through villages and past the island’s colourful seaweed farms.

Cross the famous Yellow Bridge to Nusa Ceningan for views over the turquoise lagoon, then loop back to Dream Beach and Devil’s Tear, where swells crash into the limestone cliffs and send spray high into the air — often with a rainbow.

We time the ride to finish in the late afternoon light, with a fresh coconut on the cliffs as the sun sets behind Bali.

experiences.title: Ride the Yellow Bridge
experiences.body: Pedal across the iconic bridge linking Lembongan and Ceningan above the lagoon.

experiences.title: See the Seaweed Farms
experiences.body: Learn how island families grow and dry seaweed, the traditional livelihood of Lembongan.

experiences.title: Feel the Power of Devil’s Tear
experiences.body: Watch waves explode against the cliffs — and feel the spray from a safe distance.

experiences.title: Sunset Coconut on the Cliffs
experiences.body: Finish the ride with a fresh coconut and golden light over Bali’s volcanoes.

devils-tear-island-cycling.important_notes:
The route is about 18 km with a few short hills; e-bikes are available on request.
Stay behind the safety lines at Devil’s Tear — waves can be unpredictable.
Bring sunglasses and sunscreen.

gallery.alt: Green sea turtle swimming in sunlight

gili-trawangan-turtle-snorkeling.intro: Snorkel with green and hawksbill turtles around Gili Trawangan, Gili Meno and Gili Air on a glass-bottom boat trip.
gili-trawangan-turtle-snorkeling.description:
The waters around the Gili Islands are one of the best places in Indonesia to swim with sea turtles. On this Gili Trawangan Turtle Snorkeling trip a glass-bottom boat takes you to three sites around the islands in one morning.

At Turtle Point off Gili Trawangan’s north-east coast, green and hawksbill turtles graze on seagrass in just a few metres of water. Next is the underwater Nest sculpture at Gili Meno — 48 life-size statues slowly becoming a living reef.

The trip ends on the coral gardens of Gili Air, with time for lunch on the beach before the boat returns you to Trawangan.

experiences.title: Swim with Sea Turtles
experiences.body: Float above green and hawksbill turtles as they feed on the seagrass at Turtle Point.

experiences.title: The Nest Statues at Gili Meno
experiences.body: Snorkel over the famous underwater sculptures by Jason deCaires Taylor.

experiences.title: Coral Gardens of Gili Air
experiences.body: Colourful hard corals and reef fish in calm, shallow water.

experiences.title: Glass-Bottom Boat
experiences.body: Non-swimmers can enjoy the reef through the boat’s glass floor.

gili-trawangan-turtle-snorkeling.important_notes:
Departs Gili Trawangan harbor at 10:00 AM.
Never touch or chase the turtles — give them space to breathe.
Use reef-safe sunscreen only.

gallery.alt: Rider on the beach at sunset
Riders at golden hour by the sea
Horse on the shoreline at dusk

gili-sunset-horse-riding.intro: Ride along the west coast beaches of Gili Trawangan at sunset with views of Bali’s Mount Agung and Lombok’s Rinjani.
gili-sunset-horse-riding.description:
Gili Sunset Horse Riding is the most romantic way to end a day on Gili Trawangan. Starting at the stables on the island’s quiet west side, you ride along palm-fringed paths and down to the soft sand as the sun sinks towards Bali.

Our horses are calm, well cared for and matched to your experience — complete beginners are led by a groom, while experienced riders can trot along the waterline. Mount Agung rises across the strait as the sky turns pink and gold.

The ride lasts about an hour, with stops for photos on the beach. It is suitable for riders from 8 years old and a lovely experience for couples and families.

experiences.title: Ride into the Sunset
experiences.body: Follow the west coast beach as the sun sets behind Bali’s Mount Agung.

experiences.title: For All Levels
experiences.body: Beginners are led by a groom; confident riders can trot along the shore.

experiences.title: Photo Stops on the Beach
experiences.body: Your guide takes photos of you and your horse at the best light.

experiences.title: Well-Cared-For Horses
experiences.body: Our horses are rested daily and never ridden in the midday heat.

gili-sunset-horse-riding.important_notes:
Rides start 90 minutes before sunset.
Maximum rider weight is 90 kg.
Wear long trousers and closed shoes.

top-7-unmissable-snorkeling-spots-around.hero_alt: Manta rays gliding over a coral reef off Nusa Penida
top-7-unmissable-snorkeling-spots-around.body:
From manta cleaning stations to turtle meadows, the reefs between Bali and Lombok are some of the richest in the Coral Triangle. These are the seven spots our captains and guides recommend most, with tips on when to go and who each one suits.

1. Manta Point, Nusa Penida

Reef mantas with wingspans of up to four metres visit this cleaning station almost every day of the year. Small wrasse pick parasites off their wings while snorkelers float above. Conditions can be choppy, so book a morning trip and bring a long-sleeve rash guard.

  • Best for: confident swimmers
  • Best time: 8:00–11:00 AM
  • Getting there: 35 minutes by boat from Toya Pakeh

2. Crystal Bay, Nusa Penida

A calm, sheltered bay on the west coast with excellent visibility, colourful hard corals and the chance of spotting the mola-mola (ocean sunfish) between July and October. You can snorkel straight from the beach.

3. Gamat Bay, Nusa Penida

Gentle slopes, schooling fish and a fringing reef in pristine condition make Gamat Bay perfect for beginners and families. Look for parrotfish, moorish idols and the occasional reef shark resting on the sand.

4. Mangrove Point, Nusa Lembongan

  • Best for drift snorkeling on an incoming tide.
  • Look out for turtles, batfish and giant clams.
  • Only 30 minutes by fast boat from Sanur.

5. Turtle Point, Gili Trawangan

Green and hawksbill turtles graze on the seagrass just off the north-east coast. Swim out from the beach or join a glass-bottom boat tour — and remember to give the turtles plenty of space.

6. Nest Statues, Gili Meno

Forty-eight life-size statues by Jason deCaires Taylor sit in four metres of water and are slowly becoming a living reef. Visit early in the morning for clear water and fewer boats.

7. Toyapakeh Wall, Nusa Penida

Strong currents bring nutrients that feed huge sea fans and soft corals. This is a site for confident swimmers with a guide; the boat follows you as you drift along the wall.

Snorkeling etiquette

  • Wear reef-safe sunscreen or a rash guard instead.
  • Never stand on, touch or kick the coral.
  • Keep at least three metres from mantas and turtles.
  • Book licensed operators who brief you before every swim.
Always book licensed operators, wear reef-safe sunscreen and never touch the coral or the wildlife.

best-time-of-day-for-calm-waters-crossin.hero_alt: Fast boat crossing the calm Badung Strait at sunrise
best-time-of-day-for-calm-waters-crossin.body:
The Badung Strait between Bali and Nusa Penida is only 20 kilometres wide, but it is one of the deepest channels in Indonesia. Water from the Pacific flows through it into the Indian Ocean, so tides, wind and swell can change the feel of your crossing completely. Here is how our captains choose the smoothest sailing.

Why mornings are calmer

Before the sea breeze builds, the surface of the strait is usually glassy. Most days the wind picks up after 11:00 AM and creates short, choppy waves. Departing between 7:00 and 9:00 AM gives you the calmest water and the best light for photos.

Reading the tide

When the tide runs against the wind, waves stand up and the ride gets bumpy. Captains plan departures around slack tide where possible. You do not need to read tide tables yourself — but if you are sensitive to motion, ask us which departure has the most favourable tide that day.

Seasons and swell

  • April–October (dry season): steady south-east trade winds; mornings calm, afternoons choppy.
  • November–March (wet season): lighter winds but occasional storms; crossings are often smoother outside rain squalls.
  • Big swell days: boats may land on the sheltered side of the island or delay departures for safety.

Where to sit

Choose a seat in the middle of the boat and near the back, where movement is gentlest. Keep your eyes on the horizon, avoid reading your phone and step outside for fresh air if the crew allows it.

Beating seasickness

  • Eat a light breakfast — an empty stomach makes nausea worse.
  • Take ginger candy or motion-sickness tablets 30 minutes before boarding.
  • Sit facing forward and stay hydrated.
  • Book a larger catamaran on windy days.
The best crossing is an early one: book the first or second departure of the day and you will usually arrive before the wind does.

kelingking-t-rex-cliff-diamond-beach-how.hero_alt: Kelingking T-Rex cliff above the turquoise sea
kelingking-t-rex-cliff-diamond-beach-how.body:
Kelingking’s T-Rex shaped headland and the white sand of Diamond Beach are Nusa Penida’s two most famous views — and they sit on opposite sides of the island. With an early boat and a good driver, you can see both in a single, unhurried day.

Morning: catch the first boat

Take the 7:00 or 7:30 AM fast boat from Sanur and you will land at Toya Pakeh or Banjar Nyuh before 8:30 AM. Arrange your driver in advance — they will be waiting at the harbor with your name.

Kelingking first

The drive to Kelingking takes about 50 minutes on narrow roads. Arriving before 10:00 AM means softer light, cooler temperatures and far fewer people on the viewpoint. The famous photo spot is a two-minute walk from the car park.

Should you hike down?

  • The trail to the beach is steep, partly bamboo railings and takes 30–40 minutes each way.
  • Wear proper shoes and bring at least one litre of water.
  • Swimming is dangerous because of strong waves — enjoy the sand, not the surf.

Lunch on the way east

Stop at one of the warungs near Pejukutan for nasi campur and fresh juice. The drive across the island takes about 75 minutes and passes through villages, cashew farms and hills with views of Mount Agung.

Afternoon: Diamond Beach

A staircase carved into the cliff leads down to Diamond Beach, framed by sharp limestone pinnacles. The light is beautiful in the afternoon, and neighbouring Atuh Beach is a short walk away for a swim in calmer water.

Getting back

Leave Diamond Beach by 3:30 PM to catch a 4:30 or 5:00 PM boat back to Sanur. If you would rather not rush, spend the night at a hotel in the east and visit the Tree House at sunrise.

Book your driver and the return boat before you go — on busy days the last departures sell out.

choosing-between-fast-ferry-vs-speedboat.hero_alt: Fast ferry and speedboat at a Bali harbor
choosing-between-fast-ferry-vs-speedboat.body:
All fast boats to the islands look similar from the beach, but the ride can be very different. Here is how the main types compare on comfort, speed and price so you can choose the right crossing for your trip.

Large catamarans

Twin hulls make catamarans the most stable option, especially on windy afternoons. They carry 100–200 passengers, have air-conditioned cabins and toilets, and usually board from a pier, so you keep your feet dry.

  • Crossing time: 40–50 minutes to Nusa Penida
  • Best for: families, motion-sensitive travelers, lots of luggage

Mono-hull fast boats

The most common boats on the Sanur routes. They are quick, frequent and good value, with indoor seats and an open deck at the back. On choppy days the ride feels livelier than on a catamaran.

Speedboats

Smaller boats with powerful outboard engines and 30–60 seats. They are the fastest way to cross and often land directly on the beach, which means wading in knee-deep water. Expect a bumpy, exciting ride.

Public slow ferry

The Ro-Ro car ferry from Padang Bai is the cheapest option and carries cars and motorbikes, but it takes around two hours and departure times can change at short notice.

Price comparison

  • Public ferry: from IDR 35,000 one way
  • Speedboat or mono-hull: IDR 150,000–250,000 one way
  • Catamaran: IDR 250,000–400,000 one way
  • Return tickets and hotel transfers are often bundled at a discount.

Our recommendation

Choose a catamaran for comfort, a mono-hull for value and frequent departures, and a speedboat if you want to arrive quickly and do not mind getting your feet wet. Whatever you pick, book the morning departures for the calmest water.

Penida Gili lists every operator with its vessel type, capacity and boarding style, so you know exactly what you are booking.

what-to-pack-for-an-island-getaway-to-nu.hero_alt: Yellow Bridge between Nusa Lembongan and Ceningan
what-to-pack-for-an-island-getaway-to-nu.body:
Many boats to Nusa Lembongan land directly on Jungutbatu beach, roads are narrow and the sun is strong. Packing light and smart makes the whole trip easier. This is our checklist.

The bag itself

A soft backpack or duffel is far easier than a rolling suitcase on sand and stairs. Keep it under 15 kg so the crew can pass it from boat to beach, and use a dry bag or plastic liner for your electronics.

Clothes

  • Two swimsuits so one can always dry.
  • Light, quick-dry shorts and shirts.
  • A sarong — beach towel, cover-up and temple wear in one.
  • One long-sleeve layer for the boat and the evening breeze.

Shoes

Bring sandals or water shoes you can wade in for the beach landing, plus a pair of trainers if you plan to hike to Kelingking or cycle across the Yellow Bridge to Ceningan.

Sun and sea

  • Reef-safe sunscreen (SPF 50) and a hat.
  • Polarised sunglasses for spotting turtles and mantas.
  • Your own snorkel mask if you are fussy about fit.
  • A rash guard for long snorkel trips.

Money and documents

ATMs on Lembongan sometimes run out of cash, so bring enough rupiah for small warungs and scooter rental. Keep a photo of your passport and your boat tickets on your phone.

Little extras

  • Motion-sickness tablets or ginger candy for the crossing.
  • A reusable water bottle — refill stations are everywhere.
  • Insect repellent for the mangroves at dusk.
  • A headlamp; some lanes have no street lights.
Pack half the clothes you think you need — island days are spent in a swimsuit.

balinese-cultural-etiquette-visiting-pur.hero_alt: Worshippers entering Pura Goa Giri Putri cave temple
balinese-cultural-etiquette-visiting-pur.body:
Pura Goa Giri Putri is a Hindu temple hidden inside a limestone cave on Nusa Penida’s east coast. Visitors are warmly welcomed, but temples are active places of worship. These simple customs show respect to the community and make your visit more meaningful.

Dress code

  • Wear a sarong (kamen) and a sash (selendang) — both are available to borrow at the entrance.
  • Cover your shoulders; a T-shirt is fine.
  • Remove hats and sunglasses inside the temple courtyards.

Entering the cave

The entrance to Goa Giri Putri is a narrow gap in the rock reached by a stairway of about 110 steps. Inside, the cave opens into a vast hall with shrines for Hindu, Buddhist and Chinese deities. A priest will bless you with holy water and rice at the entrance.

Behaviour inside temples

  • Speak quietly and never climb on shrines or walls.
  • Do not walk in front of people who are praying.
  • Ask before taking photos of priests or ceremonies; flash is not allowed.
  • Women who are menstruating are asked not to enter, by local custom.

Offerings

You will see small woven trays called canang sari on doorsteps, shrines and even boats. Take care not to step on them. If you would like to make your own offering, the temple guardian can sell you one at the entrance.

Donations

Entry is by donation. IDR 20,000–50,000 per person is customary and helps maintain the temple; place it in the donation box or hand it to the guardian.

Other sacred places on Nusa Penida

  • Pura Dalem Ped — the island’s most important sea temple near Ped village.
  • Pura Paluang — the “car temple” in the hills, with shrines shaped like vehicles.
  • Pura Segara Kidul — a small cliff temple above Banah.
A sarong, a smile and a small donation are all you need to be welcome in any Balinese temple.
